summary: Practise NEAT+ screening, field mitigation planning, and environmental monitoring for humanitarian projects. Explore the course outline.
lede: Environmental sustainability in humanitarian projects involves identifying and managing the effects of response and recovery activities on local resources. For project officers, field coordinators, and programme support staff, this training covers NEAT+ and FEAT screening, prioritizing site risks, and planning mitigation actions. Participants also practise tracking water, energy, and waste indicators and assigning owners and review points to environmental actions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for humanitarian professionals who shape, deliver, or support projects where site conditions, resource use, and waste decisions can affect the local environment.
modules: Climate and Environment Charter for Humanitarian Organizations
Sphere Handbook WASH and Shelter Choices
Waste Hierarchy in Humanitarian Supply Chains
Environmental Action Plans for Field Sites
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with humanitarian project cycles or field operations is helpful. No environmental-management qualification or programming experience is assumed.
